docs.title: Temporal Handling
docs.text:
Read this section before comparing any model that accepts TemporalSpec.range(...).

For most on-the-fly adapters, TemporalSpec.range(start, end) means "filter imagery in [start, end) and build one composite patch for model input," usually with median and optionally mosaic through SensorSpec.composite.

The multi-frame adapters agrifm, anysat, and galileo instead split the requested range into sub-windows and composite one frame per bin. Current single-composite adapters include remoteclip, satmae, satmaepp, satmaepp_s2_10b, scalemae, wildsat, prithvi, terrafm, terramind, dofa, fomo, thor, and satvision.

docs.title: Multi-frame Semantics
docs.text:
This section only matters for adapters that construct multi-frame inputs from one requested time window.

Shared behavior for current multi-frame adapters (agrifm, anysat, galileo):

All three split TemporalSpec.range(start, end) into T equal end-exclusive sub-windows and composite each sub-window into one frame. If a sub-window has no valid observation, the provider path reuses a fallback composite so frame count stays stable. The runtime always enforces exactly T frames; for user-provided inputs that means CHW is repeated to T and TCHW is padded or truncated to T. Frame compositing follows SensorSpec.composite, with median as the default and mosaic as the main alternative.

Per-model temporal packaging:

Model ID Frame count env (default) Temporal side input Notes agrifm RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_FRAMES (8) none (uses TCHW directly) Temporal information is encoded only in the frame stack. anysat RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_FRAMES (8) s2_dates (per-frame DOY, 0..364) DOY values are derived from each frame bin midpoint date. galileo RS_EMBED_GALILEO_FRAMES (8) months (per-frame month, 1..12) By default from frame bin midpoints; RS_EMBED_GALILEO_MONTH can force a constant month for all frames.

docs.title: Practical Guidance
docs.text: For highest reproducibility, keep each model's default normalization mode unless you can match the original training pipeline exactly. For strict-schema models such as satvision, terramind, thor, and agrifm, do not change channel order unless checkpoint metadata explicitly allows it. If you are comparing embeddings across models, standardize ROI and temporal compositing first, because preprocessing differences are substantial.

docs.title: Provenance and attribution
docs.text: Earth Embedding is an independent derivative of rs-embed, created by Dingqi Ye and contributors in the CyberGIS community. The project was developed under the GISWLH/rs-embed repository name and has been renamed GISWLH/earth-embedding. The original framework and its authors remain credited; renaming the repository does not change authorship of inherited work.

docs.title: Relationship to the upstream project
docs.text:
The upstream project established a geographic request interface for remote sensing embeddings, reusable spatial/temporal/output specifications, model adapters, data-provider integration, and batch/export workflows. This extension retains that foundation and the compatible rs_embed import path. The new earth_embedding import and earth-embedding command identify the maintained extension.

The upstream publication is:

Ye, D., Kiv, D., Hu, W., Shi, J., and Wang, S. (2026). Any Model, Any Place, Any Time: Get Remote Sensing Foundation Model Embeddings On Demand. arXiv:2602.23678.

Read the original paper. This is the original project's publication, not the Earth Embedding manuscript. No endorsement by the upstream authors is implied.

docs.title: Additions in this extension
docs.text:
Area Extension Release taxonomy Image encoders, location encoders, and precomputed products, with input-contract subclasses Location access SatCLIP integration and a shared batch coordinate API; additional GeoCLIP and lightweight Esri GLE adapters Local imagery A public image-array route with explicit spatial/temporal context and model-specific preprocessing AlphaEarth access Official GCS footprint discovery and COG point sampling, including decoding and nodata handling Research documentation Distinct global/local evaluation scopes, frozen benchmark set, and evidence boundaries Release presentation English, Chinese, and Japanese homepages; original editable Excalidraw artwork Validation Dated test and runtime receipts, with optional dependencies and access failures kept explicit

The 16 image configurations and established precomputed routes build on inherited adapters and subsequent project work. The entire model roster should not be represented as newly invented by this extension. See the changelog, source history, and individual model pages for component-level detail.

docs.title: How to cite
docs.text:
Cite Earth Embedding as software using the repository URL and the commit or release used. CITATION.cff provides metadata for this extension and references the original framework. Until a release DOI or public manuscript record exists, do not invent one.

Also cite the original rs-embed publication and each model or data publication used in the analysis. This separates framework authorship, integration work, and the scientific contribution embodied in pretrained weights or embedding products.

docs.title: Reporting lineage problems
docs.text: If an attribution, source link, or license boundary is incomplete, open an issue with the affected file and primary source. Contributions should preserve author notices, document substantial modifications, and keep checkpoint/data licensing separate from package licensing.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This page is the shortest path from installation to a first successful run. It focuses on the three core APIs most users need: get_embedding(...), get_embeddings_batch(...), and export_batch(...).

Use this page top-to-bottom once. After that, go to Models to choose model IDs, API for exact signatures and edge cases, and Extending only if you want to add a model.

Canonical model IDs use short names such as tessera, remoteclip, and prithvi. Legacy aliases such as remoteclip_s2rgb still work, but new code should use the short names.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12. Install this fork from source; pip install rs-embed installs the separate upstream distribution. earth-embedding has not yet been published to PyPI by this project.

# base install
pip install "earth-embedding @ git+https://github.com/GISWLH/earth-embedding.git"

# add [terratorch] only if you use terramind
pip install "earth-embedding[terratorch] @ git+https://github.com/GISWLH/earth-embedding.git"

For local development:

git clone https://github.com/GISWLH/earth-embedding.git
cd earth-embedding
pip install -e .  # use -e ".[terratorch]" if you need terramind

Repository examples are available in examples/playground.ipynb and examples/quickstart.py.

If this is your first time using Google Earth Engine, authenticate once:

earthengine authenticate

Earth Engine is needed only for provider-backed imagery and GSE access. Location encoders and direct AEF COG sampling work without it.

from earth_embedding import get_location_embeddings

result = get_location_embeddings("satclip", [[114.41, 30.52]], device="cpu")
print(result.data.shape)  # (1, 256), downloads weights on first use

docs.title: One place, several models
docs.text:
The same spatial and output specs work for image encoders, location encoders, and products. Use the comparison helper to collect and plot several models:

from earth_embedding import (
    BBox, OutputSpec, compare_embeddings, plot_embedding_comparison,
)

models = ["satclip", "geoclip", "esri_gle"]
comparison = compare_embeddings(
    models,
    spatial=BBox(113.9, 30.2, 114.7, 30.9),
    output=OutputSpec.grid(),
    model_options={model: {"grid_step_m": 2000} for model in models},
    device="cpu",
)
fig = plot_embedding_comparison(comparison, columns=3)
fig.savefig("location-comparison.png", dpi=180)

Install .[plot,location] for this example. It downloads location-model weights on first use and needs no Earth Engine account. See the 22-model tutorial for imagery/product models, per-model dates, failure reports, and native-resolution interpretation.

docs.title: 1. One ROI: get_embedding(...)
docs.text:
Use this when you want one embedding now.

from rs_embed import PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec, get_embedding

emb = get_embedding(
    "tessera",
    spatial=PointBuffer(lon=121.5, lat=31.2, buffer_m=1024),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.year(2024),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(pooling="mean"),
    backend="auto",
)

vec = emb.data
meta = emb.meta

Use backend="auto" unless you need to force a provider path such as backend="gee".

docs.title: 2. Many ROIs, one model: get_embeddings_batch(...)
docs.text:
Use this when the model is fixed and you have multiple ROIs.

from rs_embed import PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec, get_embeddings_batch

spatials = [
    PointBuffer(121.5, 31.2, 1024),
    PointBuffer(120.5, 30.2, 1024),
]

embs = get_embeddings_batch(
    "tessera",
    spatials=spatials,
    temporal=TemporalSpec.year(2024),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    backend="auto",
)

docs.title: 3. Dataset export: export_batch(...)
docs.text:
Use this when you are building a dataset or benchmark and want files plus manifests.

from rs_embed import (
    ExportConfig,
    ExportTarget,
    PointBuffer,
    TemporalSpec,
    export_batch,
)

spatials = [
    PointBuffer(121.5, 31.2, 1024),
    PointBuffer(120.5, 30.2, 1024),
]

export_batch(
    spatials=spatials,
    temporal=TemporalSpec.year(2024),
    models=["tessera"],
    target=ExportTarget.per_item("exports", names=["p1", "p2"]),
    backend="auto",
    config=ExportConfig(
        save_inputs=False,
        save_embeddings=True,
        resume=True,
        show_progress=True,
    ),
)

For new code, target=ExportTarget(...) plus config=ExportConfig(...) is the recommended style.

docs.title: Repository Examples
docs.text:
The repository also includes optional runnable examples:

  • examples/quickstart.py for a small end-to-end script
  • examples/playground.ipynb for notebook-style exploration

These are examples, not the primary usage path. For normal library use, start from the API snippets above.

docs.title: When You Need GEE or Model Debugging
docs.text:
Use GEE-backed on-the-fly models when you want to fetch imagery and run model inference directly. Typical examples include remoteclip, prithvi, terrafm, and terramind.

If the model output looks wrong, inspect the fetched patch before changing model settings:

inspect_provider_patch(...) is the recommended inspection API, while inspect_gee_patch(...) remains available as a compatibility alias.

docs.title: Releases and Versioning
docs.text:
Earth Embedding is an independent derivative of the upstream package. Source installation is the currently supported distribution route. PyPI publication requires configuring a new trusted publisher for GISWLH/earth-embedding; the workflow's publish jobs are disabled unless the repository variable EARTH_EMBEDDING_PYPI_ENABLED is explicitly set to true.

This page defines the release policy for earth-embedding: where users should look for changes, how version numbers move, and which kinds of changes are treated as compatibility-sensitive.

docs.title: Source of Truth
docs.text:
earth-embedding keeps a repository-level CHANGELOG as the canonical release record.

GitHub Releases should mirror the matching changelog entry for each tagged version. This avoids a split workflow where the repository says one thing and the release page says another.

In practice:

  1. Update CHANGELOG.md
  2. Bump the package version
  3. Run the manual TestPyPI publish workflow for the candidate version
  4. Create a Git tag such as v0.2.0
  5. Let the tag-triggered release workflow publish to PyPI and then create the GitHub Release from the matching CHANGELOG.md entry

docs.title: Versioning Policy
docs.text: The project follows Semantic Versioning, but uses a stricter interpretation than a typical early-stage research package because users depend on stable API and embedding semantics.

docs.title: Patch Releases
docs.text:
Use PATCH for changes such as:

  • bug fixes
  • documentation-only improvements
  • internal refactors that do not change public behavior
  • packaging or CI fixes that do not affect runtime semantics

Example: 0.1.0 -> 0.1.1

docs.title: Minor Releases
docs.text:
Use MINOR for backward-compatible feature work such as:

  • adding a new model adapter
  • adding a new public API that does not break existing callers
  • adding new optional parameters with compatible defaults
  • improving defaults without breaking existing results contracts

Example: 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0

docs.title: Major Releases
docs.text:
Use MAJOR for breaking changes such as:

  • removing or renaming a public API
  • removing or renaming a public model ID
  • changing a return type, output field, or shape contract
  • changing the default semantics of an existing model in a way that can invalidate prior experiments

Example: 1.4.2 -> 2.0.0

docs.title: Pre-1.0 Rule
docs.text:
The current package metadata still marks the library as alpha. Even so, breaking changes should not be hidden inside patch releases.

Before 1.0, the project should treat compatibility conservatively:

  • use PATCH only for safe fixes
  • use MINOR when a change is user-visible, even if Python signatures stay the same
  • clearly call out any migration work in the changelog and GitHub Release

This means 0.y.z releases should already feel predictable to downstream users.

docs.title: What Counts as a Breaking Change Here
docs.text:
For a normal Python library, breakage is often just an import or signature issue. For earth-embedding, model behavior matters just as much as function signatures.

The following should be treated as compatibility-sensitive and called out explicitly:

  • changing default preprocessing, normalization, or pooling for an existing model
  • changing the default sensor, band order, temporal window interpretation, or compositing behavior
  • changing the meaning or layout of grid or pooled outputs
  • changing model-specific defaults in a way that can alter benchmark comparability
  • removing a previously documented alias or adapter

If a user could rerun the same script and get embeddings with meaningfully different semantics, that change should be treated like a breaking API change even when the call signature looks identical.

docs.title: Release Checklist
docs.text:
For each package release:

  1. Move notable changes from Unreleased into a dated version section in CHANGELOG.md
  2. Bump src/rs_embed/_version.py
  3. Merge any required changelog updates before cutting the release tag
  4. Run release.yml manually to publish the candidate build to TestPyPI
  5. Confirm the TestPyPI smoke test can install, import, and invoke the earth-embedding CLI for rs-embed==X.Y.Z
  6. Tag the release as vX.Y.Z
  7. Let GitHub Actions publish the package to PyPI and then create the GitHub Release
  8. If the change affects public behavior, update the relevant docs page and examples

docs.title: Package Publishing
docs.text:
earth-embedding publishes wheel and source distributions through PyPI Trusted Publishing, not long-lived API tokens.

Before the first package release:

  1. Create separate owner accounts on PyPI and TestPyPI.
  2. In GitHub, create repository environments named testpypi and pypi.
  3. Require manual approval on the pypi environment. The testpypi environment can stay unprotected.
  4. In PyPI Trusted Publishers, register package name earth-embedding for repository GISWLH/earth-embedding, workflow file release.yml, and environment pypi.
  5. In TestPyPI Trusted Publishers, register the same package and repository, but use environment testpypi.
  6. Remove any old PYPI_API_TOKEN or TEST_PYPI_API_TOKEN repository secrets if earlier experiments used token-based uploads.

After that setup:

  • Actions -> release -> Run workflow builds the current ref, uploads it to TestPyPI, and then runs a smoke test that installs the published package, imports rs_embed, and invokes rs-embed --help.
  • Pushing a tag like v0.2.0 runs the same build, checks that the tag matches src/rs_embed/_version.py, validates that CHANGELOG.md has a matching version section, publishes to PyPI, and only then creates the GitHub Release from the prevalidated release notes artifact.

For a local install check against TestPyPI, use:

python -m pip install \
  --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ \
  --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ \
  rs-embed==X.Y.Z

Package versions on PyPI and TestPyPI are immutable. If a TestPyPI dry run exposed a packaging problem after upload, fix the issue and test again with a new version number rather than trying to overwrite the same release.

docs.title: Pull Request Enforcement
docs.text:
GitHub Actions checks pull requests for changelog coverage.

The check passes when any one of the following is true:

  • CHANGELOG.md is updated in the PR
  • the PR only touches docs, tests, CI, or other explicitly exempt internal files
  • the PR has the skip-changelog label

This keeps the default behavior strict for public changes without forcing changelog edits for every maintenance-only PR.

docs.title: Where Users Should Look
docs.text:
• Repository changelog: CHANGELOG.md
  • Package index: PyPI and TestPyPI
  • Tagged releases: GitHub Releases
  • Current package version: src/rs_embed/_version.py

docs.title: Research scope and evidence
docs.text:
Earth Embedding connects manuscript work to reusable software through a release-object taxonomy, explicit input contracts, and documented extraction provenance. The repository's implementation scope and the manuscript's evaluated system set are tracked separately.

The manuscript is being developed for submission to Remote Sensing of Environment. This page is not a claim of acceptance, publication, completed review, or final comparative rankings. The rs-embed paper belongs to the original CyberGIS project and must not be presented as our manuscript.

docs.title: Taxonomy based on the delivered object
docs.text:
Class What the user receives Query input Subclasses A · Image encoders Weights and preprocessing contract Satellite pixels A1 RGB; A2 fixed-schema multispectral; A3 channel-adaptive; A4 multitemporal sequence B · Location encoders A learned location-mapping network Longitude and latitude SatCLIP, GeoCLIP, Esri Global Location Encoder are examples C · Precomputed embedding products Spatially indexed embedding vectors A point or bounding box C1 gridded fields; C2 sampled collections

Class assignment follows the specific release and evaluated configuration. An image model and a derived precomputed product can belong to different classes. Temporal input takes precedence over spectral flexibility when assigning an A subclass. Architecture, training objective, output geometry, spatial support, and temporal coverage are facets, rather than competing top-level categories. Eligibility for a controlled comparison is a separate status.

The manuscript taxonomy was frozen on 2026-10-09. Changes to the software catalog do not silently revise that decision.

docs.title: Evaluated systems and integrations
docs.text:
The frozen benchmark set contains 20 systems:

  • A1, five: RemoteCLIP, SatMAE, SatMAE++ RGB, Scale-MAE, WildSAT.
  • A2, five: SatMAE++ Sentinel-2 10-band, Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind, TerraFM, SatVision-TOA.
  • A3, three: DOFA, FoMo, THOR.
  • A4, three: Galileo, AnySat, AgriFM.
  • B, one: SatCLIP, with the configured checkpoint/variant recorded in each run.
  • C1, three: GSE (AlphaEarth Foundations v2.1 annual), TESSERA v1.1, Copernicus-Embed-025deg.

The software catalog adds GeoCLIP and Esri GLE, bringing it to 22 adapters. They are not automatically included in the frozen benchmark. C2 is part of the taxonomy; this release does not claim an implemented C2 adapter or a benchmarked C2 system.

SatVision-TOA and Copernicus-Embed keep their A2 and C1 assignments even when they are ineligible for a particular controlled comparison because spatial support is unmatched. A raster resampling operation does not remove this mismatch.

docs.title: Global and local evaluation
docs.text:
The revised main design uses globally distributed 640 m spatial units. It is intended to support comparisons across geographic contexts with documented label joins, matched support, and spatial holdouts. Model availability, task eligibility, and the completeness of extracted data must be recorded before reporting comparative results.

Wuhan provides local and historical diagnostic materials, including a 567-tile subset and a 2,173-tile ROI design. These scopes have different extents and completion states. The existence of a manifest does not establish that all embeddings were extracted; results for the 567-tile subset do not establish results for the full ROI. Local results do not substitute for evidence from the revised global design.

Evaluation dimension Intended question Required evidence Land-cover classification Are pooled features useful for semantic discrimination? Label provenance, spatial split, fixed estimator/protocol Fraction regression Do features capture built-up, vegetation, and water composition? Support-matched fractions, held-out predictions, metric definition Water masks / segmentation Do available dense features retain spatial structure? Dense-output eligibility, geometry alignment, task-specific evaluation Retrieval and map inspection Which similarities or geographic patterns are represented? Defined query/gallery scope and documented qualitative selection Access and computation What does a reproducible extraction require? Checkpoints, data source, bytes, cache state, runtime, hardware, failures

These dimensions describe the evaluation framework. This page does not assert that every model has completed every task.

docs.title: What is reusable in the library?
docs.text:
The model catalog exposes input differences rather than hiding them. get_image_embedding supports user-provided imagery; get_location_embeddings provides a common location query; geographic and precomputed routes preserve source metadata. Direct AEF COG access enables workflows outside Earth Engine while retaining the official quantization and masking conventions.

For a reproducible experiment, save the repository commit, exact model/checkpoint revision, input bands and units, temporal window, spatial support, query geometry, provider/data version, output metadata, spatial split, and downstream estimator settings. Record failures and exclusions explicitly. A model that cannot access its data in one environment should not be silently converted into a scientific exclusion.

docs.title: Run a small evaluation on your own features
docs.text:
The repository's evaluation script compares saved NPZ feature matrices against a metadata CSV. Each NPZ contains X and sample_id; metadata contains sample_id,target,split,spatial_group. Supply an externally defined spatial holdout with train and test rows and disjoint spatial groups.

python -m pip install -e ".[benchmark]"
python examples/evaluate_embeddings.py --metadata metadata.csv --features satclip=satclip.npz geoclip=geoclip.npz --task classification --out evaluation.json

The script retains a common finite cohort across models, aligns rows by ID, checks group separation, fits scaling and a linear estimator on training rows only, and records input/cohort hashes. Regression is available through --task regression. Users provide task labels, features, and a meaningful split. This executable example is not a reproduction of manuscript scores.

docs.title: Reading validation correctly
docs.text:
The validation report distinguishes software regression tests, actual model inference, and live provider queries. A mocked dependency test checks error handling or interface behavior. A successful inference checks that one configuration produces a valid output. A live GCS query checks one data path. None of these by itself establishes downstream accuracy, fairness of a comparison, or a final scientific claim.

When citing the project, cite this software version, the upstream framework, and the individual model/data sources actually used. A separate manuscript citation will be added when a public bibliographic record is available. See provenance.

docs.title: Validation and current limits
docs.text:
On 2026-10-13, all 16 image encoders and SatCLIP completed a real pretrained forward pass on CPU. GeoCLIP and Esri GLE passed real-checkpoint tests, and AlphaEarth / GSE passed a live Google Cloud Storage point query. This gives 20 PASS / 2 BLOCKED across the 22-entry software catalog. Tessera and Copernicus remain blocked in the checked environments; they are not advertised as having passed pretrained inference or product access.

These are software smoke checks, not scientific benchmark results. Synthetic imagery is suitable for checking checkpoint loading, tensor handling, and finite outputs; it says nothing about representation quality, accuracy, or generalization. Additional integrations do not change the paper's frozen 20-system benchmark.

docs.title: Comparison gallery and unified API checks
docs.text:
The 22-model gallery adds a different evidence layer: 19 retained historical Wuhan image/product outputs, plus fresh SatCLIP, GeoCLIP and Esri GLE coordinate inference. It does not turn the blocked live Tessera/Copernicus access checks below into passes. Dates and spatial support differ; the historical SatVision proxy input is labeled, and the coarse Copernicus window is displayed without duplicating overlapping product cells.

The new compare_embeddings CLI was also executed with real weights for all three location encoders on CPU, with identical 320 m query settings. It returned 672 coordinate samples per model and saved real feature arrays, a combined PNG, and a run report. The comparison notebook receipt records its separate 5 km, three-model execution; full 22-model extraction in that notebook remains an optional, unexecuted cell.

Regression checks for this change passed on Windows/Python 3.13 (774 passed, 1 skipped) and Linux/Python 3.12 (773 passed, 2 skipped). Tests cover shared location sampling, finite spacing and size limits, explicit failure reports, per-model dates, visualization shapes, and offline resource discovery. Gallery source hashes and provenance document the displayed data independently of those interface tests.

docs.title: Per-model evidence
docs.text:
PASS means a real pretrained output or real product array was returned and checked for shape, nonempty values, and finiteness. BLOCKED means an external dependency, data access, or bounded runtime prevented that check. Interface tests and mocks do not qualify as a real inference PASS.

synthetic 3-band input satmaepp A1 PASS (1024,) Cached official weights; synthetic 3-band input scalemae A1 PASS (1024,) Official binary checkpoint; strict loading with modern Hub compatibility fallback wildsat A1 PASS (256,) Cached published checkpoint; synthetic 3-band input satmaepp_s2_10b A2 PASS (1024,) Explicit locally cached official Sentinel checkpoint; supplied-pixel helper prithvi A2 PASS (768,) Default EO v2 100M TL weights; synthetic 6-band input terramind A2 PASS (384,) Default small checkpoint; synthetic 12-band input terrafm A2 PASS (768,) Default base checkpoint; synthetic S2 input satvision A2 PASS (4096,) Published giant checkpoint; adapter preprocessing and pooled output dofa A3 PASS (768,) Official checkpoint; default multispectral schema fomo A3 PASS (768,) Cached published checkpoint; default band schema thor A3 PASS (768,) THOR 1.0 base checkpoint; default band schema galileo A4 PASS (128,) Cached checkpoint; independent synthetic temporal frames anysat A4 PASS (768,) Cached checkpoint; independent synthetic temporal frames agrifm A4 PASS (1024,) Cached AgriFM checkpoint; independent synthetic temporal frames satclip B PASS (256,) Default ViT16-L40 location branch; The output widths above are the observed configured outputs, not universal dimensions for every variant or pooling choice. For example, RemoteCLIP's patch features differ from its projected image embedding.

Machine-readable evidence: 22-model matrix and live AEF GCS receipt, plus the Esri real-weight receipt. The public matrix records the latest completed result, bounded failures, input/output hashes, runtime versions, and reproducible settings without publishing local host paths or raw runtime logs. Earlier failures were retained privately and superseded only after successful real reruns. Product SDKs control their own network connections independently of the runner's Hugging Face offline switch.

docs.title: Reproduce a real-weight smoke check
docs.text:
Use an environment containing the relevant model dependencies and official cached weights. The checked Linux environment used Python 3.12.2, PyTorch 2.12.0+cu130, Transformers 5.9.0, timm 1.0.15, and four CPU threads. GPU visibility was disabled for these runs. This records an environment that passed; it is not a claim that every optional model works with every possible dependency combination.

python scripts/validate_models.py --model remoteclip --model satclip --timeout 180

The runner uses a deterministic seed (20261013), raw input values in [500, 4500], the declared band order, and 64 × 64 supplied pixels before the model's own preprocessing. A4 models receive distinct frames, rather than a repeated static image. The geographic metadata is a 320 m radius around (114.35, 30.50), with the 2021 calendar year. Full input hashes, shapes, metadata, versions, durations, and output hashes are retained in the receipts. Each model runs in a fresh process with a 180 s default bound, releasing its model memory when it exits.

Hugging Face and Esri GLE runs are cache-only by default. Add --allow-network to allow their checkpoint downloads. Real product queries require --include-products; their SDKs may contact their official endpoints. Product checks are not synthetic inference:

python scripts/validate_models.py --model tessera --model copernicus \
  --include-products --allow-network --timeout 60

Copernicus uses a 0.5° bounding box in the current runner, because its native grid is 0.25° and a 640 m ROI cannot satisfy its pixel-selection contract. For an already downloaded file, set RS_EMBED_COP_DIR; for a retained GeoTessera cache, set RS_EMBED_TESSERA_CACHE. No cache was fabricated from scientific result vectors. For the verified AEF path, see direct Google Cloud Storage access.

The SatMAE++ Sentinel smoke used the existing downloaded checkpoint through RS_EMBED_SATMAEPP_S2_CKPT_FILE. Supply your own local official checkpoint path when the default Hub reference cannot be resolved; no randomly initialized model is substituted. The final ScaleMAE pass used its canonical Hub ID and cached pytorch_model.bin, with strict parameter matching.

docs.title: GeoCLIP and Esri details
docs.text:
GeoCLIP used official geoclip==1.2.3 on local CPU / Python 3.13.12. Three points (Wuhan, Tokyo, New York) produced distinct finite vectors. The maximum absolute difference from the upstream LocationEncoder was 2.60770320892334e-08, within rtol=atol=1e-5. The official bundled checkpoint SHA-256 was 94b80ae3af89fca78539e129dd2929d321247f5ceeeb0a31bc2c31041a253394.

Esri GLE now loads the official satclip.pth directly with PyTorch and the MIT-licensed SatCLIP architecture. The checkpoint has 541,440 parameters and occupies 2,168,415 bytes. Its SHA-256 is 2d5b8ac88b4a7f210a00f7fbe145f5216987f373062ec71f3065f9ba13b15452. Seven coordinates, including Wuhan, Tokyo, New York, Sydney, the equator and both poles, produced finite vectors on Linux CPU. The output matched the official package's mathematical classes with maximum absolute difference 0.0 after float32 conversion. This reference check covers the location model, not ArcGIS feature-class conversion or ArcGIS Pro integration.

The run explicitly blocked ArcGIS and ArcPy imports. It verified a fresh official download, cached .pth and explicit .dlpk use with network calls blocked, batch sizes 1/3/1024, a pooled point and a north-up (256, 3, 2) query grid. The earlier ArcGIS SDK import failure was an unnecessary integration dependency; the lightweight path supersedes that attempt. See the Esri setup guide for offline and cache options.

python scripts/validate_models.py --model esri_gle --allow-network --timeout 60

docs.title: Regression and compatibility checks
docs.text:
The full Linux release suite passed; the unit-test receipt records the exact final count, skipped tests, versions, and elapsed time. Targeted checks for the ScaleMAE binary fallback also passed 2 tests. Tests using substitutes verify contracts only and are kept separate from the real-weight results above.

This work also fixed five adapters that previously initialized an imagery provider even when pixels were supplied: RemoteCLIP, Prithvi, DOFA, TerraMind, and TerraFM. The no-provider regression reproduced five failures before the fix and passed afterward. The new get_image_embedding helper has 16 contract tests, with real pretrained helper calls additionally verified for RemoteCLIP, ScaleMAE, and SatMAE++ Sentinel. The helper requires the spatial/time context and preserves raw sensor preprocessing inside each model adapter.

Remaining scope: authenticated Earth Engine data access, Esri GPU inference, Tessera/Copernicus product access in a connected data environment, additional checkpoint variants, all grid/batch combinations, and downstream scientific performance have not all been validated by this smoke pass.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: This page is a recipe collection for common tasks after you already know the basic APIs. Use Quickstart for the first-run path and API for exact signatures.

docs.title: One ROI Prototype
docs.text:
Use get_embedding(...) when you want one ROI embedding now and want the smallest possible call.

from rs_embed import FetchSpec, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec, get_embedding

emb = get_embedding(
    "remoteclip",
    spatial=PointBuffer(lon=121.5, lat=31.2, buffer_m=2048),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-06-01", "2022-09-01"),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    fetch=FetchSpec(scale_m=10),
    backend="auto",
    device="auto",
)

This is the right path when you are prototyping, inspecting metadata, debugging one location, or applying a quick sampling override through fetch=FetchSpec(...).

docs.title: Many ROIs, One Model
docs.text:
Use get_embeddings_batch(...) when the model is fixed and you have multiple ROIs.

from rs_embed import PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec, get_embeddings_batch

spatials = [
    PointBuffer(121.5, 31.2, 2048),
    PointBuffer(120.5, 30.2, 2048),
]

embs = get_embeddings_batch(
    "remoteclip",
    spatials=spatials,
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-06-01", "2022-09-01"),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    backend="auto",
)

This path is best when the model is fixed, the ROI list is larger than one point, and you want simpler code than a manual loop while still benefiting from any embedder-level batch inference.

docs.title: Build a Dataset Export
docs.text:
Use export_batch(...) for reproducible data pipelines and downstream experiments. For new code, prefer target=ExportTarget(...) plus config=ExportConfig(...).

from rs_embed import FetchSpec, export_batch, ExportConfig, ExportTarget, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec

spatials = [
    PointBuffer(121.5, 31.2, 2048),
    PointBuffer(120.5, 30.2, 2048),
]

export_batch(
    spatials=spatials,
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-06-01", "2022-09-01"),
    models=["remoteclip", "prithvi"],
    target=ExportTarget.per_item("exports", names=["p1", "p2"]),
    fetch=FetchSpec(scale_m=10),
    backend="auto",
    config=ExportConfig(save_inputs=True, save_embeddings=True, resume=True),
)

Stable ROI names make exports and manifests easier to track. Keep one temporal policy across all items for fair comparisons, and mix multiple models in one job when you are building benchmark datasets. per_item keeps each ROI grouped together, which helps with inspection and resume. Move runtime knobs into ExportConfig(...) rather than adding more top-level keywords, and use one shared FetchSpec when you want to normalize resolution or compositing across models.

docs.title: Inspect Inputs Before Modeling
docs.text: Use patch inspection when outputs look suspicious (clouds, wrong band order, bad dynamic range, etc.).

docs.title: Preferred: provider-agnostic
docs.text:
from rs_embed import inspect_provider_patch, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, SensorSpec

report = inspect_provider_patch(
    spatial=PointBuffer(121.5, 31.2, 2048),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-06-01", "2022-09-01"),
    sensor=SensorSpec(
        collection="COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED",
        bands=("B4", "B3", "B2"),
        scale_m=10,
    ),
    backend="gee",
)

docs.title: Backward-compatible alias
docs.text: inspect_gee_patch(...) calls the same underlying inspection flow for GEE paths.

docs.title: Large ROI with Tiling
docs.text:
If you request large ROIs for on-the-fly models, try API-side tiling:

from rs_embed import get_embedding, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec

emb = get_embedding(
    "remoteclip",
    spatial=PointBuffer(121.5, 31.2, 8000),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-06-01", "2022-09-01"),
    output=OutputSpec.grid(),
    backend="auto",
    input_prep="tile",
)

Use input_prep="tile" when OutputSpec.grid() matters, when a large-ROI resize would lose too much detail, and when you accept extra runtime cost in exchange for better spatial structure preservation.

docs.title: Fair Cross-Model Comparison
docs.text:
When benchmarking models, keep the ROI list, temporal window, and compositing policy fixed, start with OutputSpec.pooled(), and prefer each model's default normalization unless you are deliberately replicating an original training setup.

Then use Supported Models to review model-specific preprocessing and required side inputs.

docs.title: earth-embedding visual identity
docs.text:
The mark is a hand-sketched globe inside vector brackets whose lower-right edge breaks into a few embedding cells: Earth, encoded. The banner tells the same story as a sketch, with imagery, places and products flowing through get_embedding() into a vector and an embedding space where similar places cluster. Ink teal, sage and a small terracotta accent on warm paper keep every asset in one family. Every scene sits on its own paper card, so it reads on light and dark pages alike.

All marks, shapes, arrows and text are native editable Excalidraw elements. Open the .excalidraw files in Excalidraw to change the artwork. The drawings contain no raster background or AI-generated image. The A/B/C labels follow the project's release taxonomy; C2 is a taxonomy category, not a claim that a particular C2 product is implemented. Downstream tasks describe what users can build with suitable features and task-specific methods.

docs.text:

node scripts/render_brand.mjs --only banner,logo
python scripts/optimize_images.py docs/assets/brand

The script builds each scene from code and exports it with Excalidraw's own convertToExcalidrawElements, exportToSvg and exportToBlob APIs in headless Chromium. The Vite server binds only to 127.0.0.1 and closes after rendering. Development dependencies are isolated under work/brand; the Python package does not depend on them.

SVG exports embed Excalifont, Nunito and Cascadia font subsets, so they render the same on GitHub and the documentation site. Review screenshots of the banner (900 px and 390 px, on a dark page), both diagrams and the logo at 32–180 px are written to work/brand.

docs.title: AgriFM (agrifm)
docs.text: Multi-frame Sentinel-2 adapter for AgriFM (Video Swin-style backbone), with fixed-frame temporal packaging and provider-backed S2 sequence fetching.

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text: Field Value Model ID agrifm Family / Backbone AgriFM (vendored Video Swin runtime + checkpoint loader) Adapter type on-the-fly Typical backend provider backend (gee) Primary input S2 SR 10-band time series (T,10,H,W) Default resolution 10m default provider fetch (sensor.scale_m) Temporal mode range in practice (window split into T frames) Output modes pooled, grid Extra side inputs none required (adapter builds fixed frame stack) Training alignment (adapter path) High when n_frames, normalization, and checkpoint version are fixed

docs.title: When To Use This Model
docs.text: AgriFM is a good fit for crop-oriented temporal S2 experiments, comparisons against other multi-frame adapters such as anysat and galileo, and workflows where a fixed-length frame stack is useful. The main pitfalls are changing RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_FRAMES between runs, forgetting that CHW inputs are repeated to T frames, and comparing it to single-window models without documenting the temporal packaging.

docs.title: Spatial / temporal
docs.text: AgriFM is provider-backed, so use backend="gee" or another provider-compatible backend. TemporalSpec is normalized to a range through the shared helper, and TemporalSpec.range(...) is the clearest choice. The provider path fetches a multi-frame S2 sequence over that range and composes it into a fixed T-frame stack.

docs.title: Sensor / channels
docs.text:
If sensor is omitted, AgriFM uses COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED with bands B2,B3,B4,B5,B6,B7,B8,B8A,B11,B12, scale_m=10, cloudy_pct=30, composite="median", and fill_value=0.0.

For input_chw, the adapter accepts CHW with C=10 and repeats that frame to T = RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_FRAMES, or TCHW with C=10 and pads or truncates to the exact configured frame count. Values are clipped to the raw S2 SR range 0..10000.

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline (Current rs-embed Path)
docs.text:
SETUP  runtime settings
  -> n_frames + image_size + normalization mode
  -> checkpoint path (local or auto-download)
INPUT  provider fetch / input_chw
  -> multi-frame raw TCHW
     input_chw path: coerce CHW / TCHW to exact T
  -> optional inspection on frame 0
  -> normalize with RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_NORM
     agrifm_stats: z-score with AgriFM S2 statistics
     unit_scale: /10000 -> clip [0,1]
     none / raw: keep clipped raw values
  -> resize all frames to RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_IMG=224
  -> load checkpoint + vendored runtime
  -> forward to embedding grid (D,H,W)
  -> output projection
     pooled: spatial mean / max over grid
     grid:   xarray.DataArray

docs.title: Temporal / preprocessing
docs.text: Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_FRAMES 8 Fixed frame count T RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_IMG 224 Resize target image size RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_NORM agrifm_stats agrifm_stats, unit_scale, or none RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_FETCH_WORKERS 8 Provider prefetch workers for batch APIs

docs.title: Checkpoint loading
docs.text: Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_CKPT unset Local checkpoint path RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_AUTO_DOWNLOAD 1 Allow checkpoint auto-download RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_CACHE_DIR ~/.cache/rs_embed/agrifm Checkpoint cache dir RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_CKPT_FILE AgriFM.pth Cached checkpoint filename RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_CKPT_URL project default URL Checkpoint download URL RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_CKPT_MIN_BYTES large-size threshold Download validation threshold

docs.title: Output Semantics
docs.text: AgriFM uses the standard feature-grid pattern for multi-frame encoders. pooled applies spatial pooling over the model feature grid, and grid returns (D,H,W) in model feature-map space rather than georeferenced raster pixels. The useful model-specific details are mostly carried in metadata, including frame count and normalization settings.

docs.title: Minimal provider-backed example
docs.text:
from rs_embed import get_embedding, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec

emb = get_embedding(
    "agrifm",
    spatial=PointBuffer(lon=121.5, lat=31.2, buffer_m=2048),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-01-01", "2022-12-31"),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    backend="gee",
)

docs.title: Example temporal packaging and normalization tuning
docs.text:
# Example (shell):
# export RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_FRAMES=8
# export RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_IMG=224
# export RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_NORM=agrifm_stats

docs.title: Common Failure Modes / Debugging
docs.text:
• backend mismatch (agrifm is provider-only)
  • wrong input_chw shape (must be CHW/TCHW with C=10)
  • silent temporal mismatch from CHW repeat-to-T behavior
  • checkpoint download failure or invalid local checkpoint path
  • missing lightweight import deps (torch, timm, einops) for vendored backbone import

Recommended first checks:

Inspect metadata for n_frames, norm_mode, input_frames, and grid_hw first. Verify whether the input came from provider fetch or from repeated CHW, and pin the checkpoint source or path before benchmarking.

docs.title: Reproducibility Notes
docs.text: Keep RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_FRAMES, RS_EMBED_AGRIFM_IMG, normalization mode, checkpoint source or path, temporal window, compositing settings, and output mode fixed and recorded. Multi-frame models are very sensitive to frame count and frame construction, so changing FRAMES is a different experiment rather than a small tuning tweak.

docs.title: Source of Truth (Code Pointers)
docs.text: The main code paths are src/rs_embed/embedders/catalog.py for registration, src/rs_embed/embedders/onthefly_agrifm.py for the adapter, and src/rs_embed/embedders/runtime_utils.py for shared temporal fetch and coercion helpers.

docs.title: AnySat (anysat)
docs.text: Multi-frame Sentinel-2 time-series adapter that builds AnySat inputs (s2 + s2_dates) from a temporal window and returns dense sub-patch grids by default or pooled vectors.

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text: Field Value Model ID anysat Family / Backbone AnySat (vendored local runtime) Adapter type on-the-fly Typical backend provider-backed; prefer backend="auto" in public API Primary input S2 10-band time series (T,C,H,W) Default resolution 10m default provider fetch (sensor.scale_m) Temporal mode range in practice (adapter normalizes year/None to range) Output modes pooled, grid Model config keys variant (default: base; choices: base) Extra side inputs required s2_dates (per-frame DOY values) Training alignment (adapter path) Medium (depends on frame count, normalization mode, and image size)

docs.title: When To Use This Model
docs.text: AnySat is a good fit when you want actual temporal S2 sequence modeling rather than a single composite, when day-of-year context matters, or when you are explicitly comparing multi-frame adapters such as anysat, galileo, and agrifm. It becomes easy to misuse if you compare it against single-composite models without matching temporal assumptions, if you change frame count or normalization without recording it, or if you read grid output as a georeferenced raster instead of model patch output.

docs.title: Spatial / temporal
docs.text: The adapter accepts BBox and PointBuffer, and normalizes TemporalSpec to a range internally; using TemporalSpec.range(...) directly is still the clearest and most reproducible choice. The requested window is split into T sub-windows, one composite is built per bin, and the midpoint of each bin is converted into AnySat-style day-of-year values in s2_dates.

docs.title: Sensor / channels
docs.text:
If sensor is omitted, AnySat uses COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED with bands ("B2","B3","B4","B5","B6","B7","B8","B8A","B11","B12"), scale_m=10, cloudy_pct=30, composite="median", and fill_value=0.0.

For input_chw, the adapter accepts either CHW or TCHW with C=10. A CHW tensor is repeated to T frames, while TCHW is padded or truncated to the exact configured frame count. Values are clipped to the raw-SR range 0..10000.

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline (Current rs-embed Path)
docs.text:
INPUT  provider fetch / input_chw
  -> S2 10-band time series in TCHW
     input_chw path: coerce CHW / TCHW to exact T
  -> optional resize to RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_IMG=24
  -> normalize series with RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_NORM
     per_tile_zscore: default
     unit_scale / reflectance: /10000 -> [0,1]
     raw / none: keep raw values
  -> build AnySat side inputs
     s2: [1,T,10,H,W]
     s2_dates: [1,T] from frame-bin DOY midpoints
  -> forward with AnySat spatial output
     grid path: default `output="dense"` (`grid_feature_mode="dense"`)
     pooled path: default compatibility path keeps `output="patch"`; optional `pooled_source="tile"` uses native AnySat tile output
  -> map [B,H,W,D] -> rs-embed grid [D,H,W]
  -> output projection
     pooled: spatial mean / max over patch grid
     grid:   dense sub-patch grid by default (or patch grid when overridden)

Important constraint:

sensor.scale_m or fetch.scale_m must be a positive multiple of 10 meters.

docs.title: Environment Variables / Tuning Knobs
docs.text: Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_FRAMES 8 Number of temporal frames T RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_IMG 24 Per-frame resize target (square) RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_NORM per_tile_zscore Series normalization mode RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_MODEL_SIZE base AnySat model size RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_GRID_MODE dense Grid path native AnySat spatial output (dense or patch) RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_POOLED_SOURCE patch Pooled path source (patch compatibility pooling or native tile) RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_FLASH_ATTN 0 Enable flash attention path if supported RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_PRETRAINED 1 Load pretrained checkpoint weights RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_CKPT unset Local checkpoint override RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_HF_REPO g-astruc/AnySat Hugging Face repo used for checkpoint download RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_HF_FILE models/AnySat.pth Checkpoint file inside the Hugging Face repo RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_CACHE_DIR ~/.cache/rs_embed/anysat Checkpoint cache dir RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_CKPT_MIN_BYTES adapter threshold Download size sanity check RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_FETCH_WORKERS 8 Provider prefetch workers for batch APIs

docs.title: Output Semantics
docs.text: AnySat now uses two spatial output paths inside the adapter. pooled defaults to the historical rs-embed behavior and applies spatial pooling over the AnySat patch grid, which preserves the previous pooled vector dimensionality; pass pooled_source="tile" (or set RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_POOLED_SOURCE=tile) to use the native AnySat tile embedding instead. grid defaults to AnySat dense, so the returned (D,H,W) is a denser sub-patch feature map by default; pass grid_feature_mode="patch" to the public API (or set RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_GRID_MODE=patch) to recover the older patch-grid behavior. As with other on-the-fly models, this grid is model space rather than guaranteed georeferenced raster pixels.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
from rs_embed import get_embedding, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec

emb = get_embedding(
    "anysat",
    spatial=PointBuffer(lon=121.5, lat=31.2, buffer_m=2048),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-01-01", "2023-01-01"),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    backend="auto",
)

docs.title: Example with temporal/frame tuning (env-controlled)
docs.text:
# Example (shell):
# export RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_FRAMES=8
# export RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_NORM=per_tile_zscore
# export RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_IMG=24

docs.title: Common Failure Modes / Debugging
docs.text:
• backend is not provider-compatible
  • wrong channel count for input_chw (must be 10 channels)
  • fetch.scale_m / sensor.scale_m is not a positive multiple of 10
  • missing torch / einops / huggingface_hub dependency for vendored runtime + checkpoint path
  • local checkpoint missing / too small / invalid format
  • inconsistent results from untracked changes to FRAMES, NORM, or image size

Recommended first check:

Inspect the input patches first and confirm that the temporal window and frame construction match the experiment you think you are running.

docs.title: Reproducibility Notes
docs.text: For fair comparisons and stable reruns, record the temporal window, RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_FRAMES, RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_NORM, RS_EMBED_ANYSAT_IMG, the effective provider resolution from fetch.scale_m or sensor.scale_m, and the exact checkpoint source.

docs.title: Source of Truth (Code Pointers)
docs.text: The main code paths are src/rs_embed/embedders/catalog.py for registration, src/rs_embed/embedders/onthefly_anysat.py for the adapter, and src/rs_embed/embedders/runtime_utils.py for TCHW coercion helpers.

docs.title: Copernicus Embed (copernicus)
docs.text: Precomputed embedding adapter using a vendored local GeoTIFF reader over the published torchgeo/copernicus_embed Hugging Face dataset, with strict bbox slicing.

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text: Field Value Model ID copernicus Aliases copernicus_embed Family / Source torchgeo/copernicus_embed GeoTIFF redistribution on Hugging Face Adapter type precomputed Typical backend auto Primary input BBox / PointBuffer in EPSG:4326, sliced via vendored GeoTIFF bbox indexing Product grid CRS fixed EPSG:4326 grid (not the common provider-backed EPSG:3857 default) Default resolution 0.25° source product resolution Temporal mode strict TemporalSpec.year(2021) in v0.1 Output modes pooled, grid Extra side inputs none Training alignment (adapter path) N/A (precomputed product)

docs.title: When To Use This Model
docs.text: Copernicus Embed is a good fit for precomputed embedding workflows via local GeoTIFF access, quick spatial baselines without provider requests, and experiments where coarse precomputed coverage is acceptable. It is easy to misuse if you request years other than 2021, pass ROIs smaller than one 0.25° pixel, or use non-auto backends.

docs.title: Spatial
docs.text:
The adapter accepts BBox directly and PointBuffer, which it converts to an EPSG:4326 bbox. Internally it slices the local GeoTIFF with bbox indexing via ds[minlon:maxlon, minlat:maxlat].

Warning

Copernicus keeps the product's fixed EPSG:4326 grid with 0.25 degree pixels. That differs from the more common provider-backed EPSG:3857 sampling default used elsewhere in rs-embed, even though the public spatial input is still EPSG:4326.

docs.title: Temporal
docs.text: Copernicus Embed requires TemporalSpec.year(...), currently supports only 2021, and validates the year before dataset access.

docs.title: Backend / data directory
docs.text: The backend should be auto, although legacy local is still accepted for compatibility. Data directory resolution comes from RS_EMBED_COP_DIR by default, or from a per-call override such as sensor.collection="dir:/path/to/copernicus_embed".

docs.title: Retrieval Pipeline (Current rs-embed Path)
docs.text:
INPUT  TemporalSpec.year(...) + SpatialSpec
  -> validate supported year
     current adapter supports 2021
  -> resolve data_dir
     default: RS_EMBED_COP_DIR
     override: sensor.collection
  -> load / cache CopernicusEmbedGeoTiff dataset
     download=True in current adapter
  -> convert SpatialSpec to EPSG:4326 bbox
  -> validate ROI covers at least one full Copernicus pixel
  -> bbox slice -> sample["image"] as CHW
  -> output projection
     pooled: vector
     grid:   embedding grid

Notes:

temporal is validated, but metadata in the current adapter is built with temporal=None, so record the requested year externally if strict provenance matters.

docs.title: Environment Variables / Tuning Knobs
docs.text:
Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_COP_DIR data/copernicus_embed Local Copernicus embed GeoTIFF directory RS_EMBED_COPERNICUS_BATCH_WORKERS 4 Batch worker count for get_embeddings_batch(...)

Non-env override:

sensor.collection="dir:/path/to/copernicus_embed" overrides the data directory per call.

Current fixed adapter behavior (not env-configurable in v0.1):

The current adapter keeps download=True, and that is not env-configurable in v0.1.

docs.title: Output Semantics
docs.text:
Copernicus follows the same precomputed-product pattern as the other local or provider-sampled embedding products. pooled applies spatial pooling over the sampled CHW embedding grid, and grid returns (D,H,W) in product space rather than raw imagery pixel space.

The current adapter exposes this explicitly in metadata: input_crs is EPSG:4326, output_crs is the fixed product CRS EPSG:4326, and product_resolution_deg records the 0.25 degree grid spacing.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
from rs_embed import get_embedding, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec

emb = get_embedding(
    "copernicus",
    spatial=PointBuffer(lon=121.5, lat=31.2, buffer_m=5000),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.year(2021),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    backend="auto",
)

docs.title: Local dataset directory override
docs.text:
# Example (shell):
# export RS_EMBED_COP_DIR=/data/copernicus_embed

docs.title: Common Failure Modes / Debugging
docs.text:
• year not supported (2021 only in current adapter)
  • backend is not auto
  • broken local install missing the GeoTIFF stack (tifffile / imagecodecs)
  • dataset files missing/corrupt under RS_EMBED_COP_DIR
  • ROI is smaller than one Copernicus pixel (raises immediately)

Recommended first checks:

Confirm TemporalSpec.year(2021) first, then inspect metadata such as data_dir, chw_shape, and bbox_4326. If coverage seems empty, test a larger ROI before assuming the dataset is broken.

docs.title: Reproducibility Notes
docs.text: Keep the dataset path or version snapshot, requested year, ROI geometry, and output mode fixed and recorded.

docs.title: Source of Truth (Code Pointers)
docs.text: The main code paths are src/rs_embed/embedders/catalog.py for registration, src/rs_embed/embedders/precomputed_copernicus_embed.py for the adapter, and src/rs_embed/embedders/_vendor/copernicus_embed.py for the vendored GeoTIFF reader.

docs.title: DOFA (dofa)
docs.text: DOFA adapter for multispectral inputs with explicit per-channel wavelengths, supporting provider and tensor backends.

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text: Field Value Model ID dofa Family / Backbone DOFA ViT (base / large, official checkpoints) Adapter type on-the-fly Typical backend provider backend (gee), also supports backend="tensor" Primary input Raw Sentinel-2 SR CHW + wavelengths (µm) Default resolution 10m default provider fetch (sensor.scale_m) Temporal mode provider path requires TemporalSpec.range(...) Output modes pooled, grid Model config keys variant (default: base; choices: base, large) Extra side inputs required wavelength vector (wavelengths_um) Training alignment (adapter path) Medium-High (when wavelengths and band semantics are correct)

docs.title: When To Use This Model
docs.text: DOFA is the right choice when wavelength-aware multispectral modeling matters, when you need custom band combinations with matching wavelengths, or when you want to compare spectral models against more S2-specific adapters. The main failure mode is semantic mismatch: missing wavelengths, wrong wavelength-to-channel alignment, or unlogged changes to variant and wavelength configuration will all make results hard to trust.

docs.title: Spatial / temporal
docs.text: The provider path requires TemporalSpec.range(start, end). The tensor path bypasses provider fetch entirely, so temporal semantics only matter insofar as they shaped the tensor you prepared.

docs.title: Sensor / channels (provider path)
docs.text:
If sensor is omitted, the provider path uses COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED with the official DOFA S2 9-band order B4,B3,B2,B5,B6,B7,B8,B11,B12, plus scale_m=10, cloudy_pct=30, composite="median", and fill_value=0.0.

Wavelengths:

The adapter requires one wavelength in micrometers per channel. If sensor.wavelengths is not provided, it tries to infer wavelengths from sensor.bands, but only known schemas such as the supported Sentinel-2 subsets are inferable. len(wavelengths_um) must always match the channel count C.

input_chw contract (provider override path):

If you override fetch with input_chw, it must be CHW with C == len(bands) and raw SR values in 0..10000.

docs.title: Tensor backend contract
docs.text: For backend="tensor", input_chw must be CHW, and batch tensor usage should go through get_embeddings_batch_from_inputs(...). sensor.bands is required so the official preprocessing path can be applied, and sensor.wavelengths should either be provided directly or be inferable from the bands. The tensor is expected to hold raw SR values in 0..10000, not pre-normalized [0,1].

docs.title: Provider path
docs.text:
PROVIDER  fetch raw multiband Sentinel-2 SR patch
  -> optional raw-value inspection
     expected_channels=len(bands), value range [0,10000]
  -> raw SR 0..10000 -> 0..255-like scale
  -> official DOFA S2 per-band mean/std normalization
  -> resize to fixed 224x224
     bilinear; no crop / pad
  -> load DOFA model variant
     variant: base | large
  -> forward(image, wavelengths)
  -> output projection
     pooled: embedding vector
     grid:   patch-token grid

docs.title: Tensor path
docs.text:
TENSOR  read raw SR input_chw
  -> reject already-normalized [0,1]-like inputs
  -> apply provider-equivalent DOFA preprocessing
     raw SR 0..10000 -> [0,1]
     rescale to 0..255-like values
     official per-band mean/std normalization
  -> resize to fixed 224x224
  -> resolve wavelengths
     preferred: sensor.wavelengths
     fallback:  infer from sensor.bands
  -> forward(image, wavelengths)
  -> output projection
     pooled: embedding vector
     grid:   patch-token grid

Fixed adapter behavior:

The current implementation fixes image size at 224, and the official preprocessing path is defined for Sentinel-2 subsets of B4,B3,B2,B5,B6,B7,B8,B11,B12.

docs.title: Environment Variables / Tuning Knobs
docs.text:
Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_DOFA_FETCH_WORKERS 8 Provider prefetch workers for batch APIs RS_EMBED_DOFA_BATCH_SIZE CPU:8, CUDA:64 Inference batch size for batch APIs RS_EMBED_DOFA_BASE_WEIGHTS unset Local override for the base checkpoint file RS_EMBED_DOFA_LARGE_WEIGHTS unset Local override for the large checkpoint file RS_EMBED_DOFA_WEIGHTS_DIR unset Directory override containing DOFA checkpoint files RS_EMBED_DOFA_HF_REPO_ID earthflow/DOFA Hugging Face repo used for checkpoint download RS_EMBED_DOFA_HF_REVISION main Hugging Face revision used for checkpoint download

Non-env model selection knobs:

The main non-env knobs are variant (base or large), sensor.bands for channel semantics and wavelength inference, and sensor.wavelengths for an explicit wavelength vector in micrometers.

If variant is omitted, rs-embed uses the base DOFA checkpoint by default. Pass variant="large" to switch to the larger model.

Quick reminder:

Pass variant directly to get_embedding("dofa", ..., variant="base"). For export jobs, use ExportModelRequest.configure("dofa", variant="large").

docs.title: Output Semantics
docs.text: DOFA mostly follows the standard pooled and token-grid pattern. pooled returns a vector (D,), while grid reshapes patch tokens to (D,H,W) in model token space rather than georeferenced raster space. The model-specific part is mainly in metadata, which records wavelengths, variant choice, and preprocessing details.

docs.title: Minimal provider-backed example (S2 wavelengths inferred automatically)
docs.text:
from rs_embed import get_embedding, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec

emb = get_embedding(
    "dofa",
    spatial=PointBuffer(lon=121.5, lat=31.2, buffer_m=2048),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-06-01", "2022-09-01"),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    backend="gee",
)

docs.title: Switch to the large checkpoint
docs.text:

emb = get_embedding(
    "dofa",
    spatial=PointBuffer(lon=121.5, lat=31.2, buffer_m=2048),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-06-01", "2022-09-01"),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    backend="gee",
    variant="large",

docs.title: Custom bands / wavelengths example (conceptual)
docs.text:
from rs_embed import SensorSpec

sensor = SensorSpec(
    collection="COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED",
    bands=("B2", "B3", "B4", "B8"),
    scale_m=10,
)
# If bands are non-standard, provide wavelengths explicitly via an extended sensor object/field used by your code path.

docs.title: Common Failure Modes / Debugging
docs.text:
• provider path called with non-range temporal spec
  • wavelength vector missing or wrong length for channel count
  • unsupported bands for the official S2 preprocessing path
  • tensor backend called with already-normalized [0,1] inputs
  • tensor backend called without input_chw
  • unknown variant (must be base or large)

Recommended first checks:

Print or log the exact bands and wavelengths_um used by the adapter, then verify that the provider or tensor input is scaled and ordered the way you intended before blaming the model.

docs.title: Reproducibility Notes
docs.text: Keep the variant, exact bands, exact wavelengths_um, temporal window and compositing policy, output mode, and backend choice fixed and recorded. Those settings materially change what DOFA sees.

docs.title: Source of Truth (Code Pointers)

docs.title: Esri Global Location Encoder (Sentinel-2)
docs.text:
esri_gle turns WGS84 longitude/latitude coordinates into 256-dimensional embeddings using Esri's official pretrained weights. The adapter runs the location encoder directly in PyTorch with the bundled MIT-licensed SatCLIP architecture. ArcGIS, ArcPy, fastai, imagery downloads and Earth Engine initialization are not required.

The model is lightweight: the official download is 3,741,098 bytes (about 3.7 MB), containing a 2,168,415-byte satclip.pth checkpoint. Esri's weights are distinct from Microsoft's SatCLIP checkpoints; this adapter uses the Esri checkpoint.

docs.title: Query
docs.text:
The base installation provides the required runtime. On first use, the adapter downloads the official model package and caches its extracted checkpoint locally.

from earth_embedding import get_location_embeddings

embedding = get_location_embeddings(
    "esri_gle",  # aliases: "esri", "global_location_encoder"
    [[114.4, 30.5], [-117.1956, 34.0564]],  # longitude, latitude
    device="cpu",
    batch_size=1024,
)
print(embedding.data.shape)  # (2, 256)
print(embedding.meta)

Input rows are preserved. The result is a finite float32 array with shape (N, 256). batch_size bounds the number of coordinates in each forward pass.

docs.title: Downloads, caching and offline use
docs.text:
The default download is the model package published through Esri's Global Location Encoder catalog item. The adapter verifies the extracted checkpoint against its pinned SHA-256 digest. It reads the checkpoint with PyTorch's weights_only=True loader and checks the parameter structure before inference. No Esri weights are bundled in this repository, and the package's bundled Python files are never executed. The outer package digest below records the checked download for reference.

Artifact Bytes SHA-256 Official catalog .dlpk 3,741,098 8bb10ad29bf9e538c7724f118dfa12ceb052b61a603ef3ca8a8819c7f1ef42fe satclip.pth 2,168,415 2d5b8ac88b4a7f210a00f7fbe145f5216987f373062ec71f3065f9ba13b15452

The default checkpoint cache is ~/.cache/earth_embedding/esri_gle/satclip.pth. Set cache_dir to choose its directory. Once populated, the same cache supports an explicitly offline call:

locations = [[114.4, 30.5], [139.76, 35.68]]

# Download the official package and cache its verified weights if needed.
get_location_embeddings(
    "esri_gle", locations, device="cpu", cache_dir="./model-cache/esri"
)

# Reuse only local files; fail clearly if the required weights are absent.
offline = get_location_embeddings(
    "esri_gle",
    locations,
    device="cpu",
    cache_dir="./model-cache/esri",
    local_files_only=True,
)

An existing official .dlpk or its extracted satclip.pth can be supplied directly. The checkpoint must match the pinned Esri weights:

offline = get_location_embeddings(
    "esri_gle",
    locations,
    checkpoint="/path/to/satclip.pth",  # or the official .dlpk
    device="cpu",
    local_files_only=True,
)

RS_EMBED_ESRI_GLE_CKPT also accepts a local checkpoint path; the explicit checkpoint argument takes precedence. Both official catalog and ArcGIS-runtime packages contain the same verified satclip.pth and are accepted.

Downloads and use remain subject to Esri's model terms. A checksum establishes artifact identity, not a different license.

docs.title: Runtime and spatial queries
docs.text:
The location branch uses L=40 spherical-harmonic features and a SIREN network. Inference uses float64 internally to follow the reference model's numerical path, then returns float32 features. Metadata records the backend, device, checkpoint provenance and coordinate order. The network has 541,440 parameters. CPU inference is supported; an explicit MPS request is rejected because MPS does not support float64. device="auto" selects CUDA when available and CPU otherwise.

On 2026-10-13, seven real coordinate queries produced finite (7, 256) vectors on CPU with ArcGIS and ArcPy imports disabled. Outputs matched the official package's mathematical implementation exactly after float32 conversion. The execution receipt also records first download, offline cache/package use, batch consistency, pooled and grid checks.

get_embedding("esri_gle", spatial=..., device="cpu") supports the same centre query interface as the other location encoders. OutputSpec.grid() samples coordinates on a north-up grid, with grid_step_m=1000 and max_grid_points=100000 defaults. These are sampling controls, not an assertion of model resolution. Requested dates are ignored.

See the validation report for dated execution evidence and the tested environments.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text: The official model is intended primarily for land locations and summarizes conditions captured by its training imagery. A coordinate query does not provide time-specific observations, arbitrary current imagery or guaranteed generalization over open ocean. This additional integration is not part of the paper's frozen 20-system benchmark.

docs.title: FoMo (fomo)
docs.text: Multispectral Sentinel-2 adapter for FoMo-Bench (MultiSpectralViT), with explicit S2 modality-key mapping and token/grid outputs averaged across spectral modalities.

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text: Field Value Model ID fomo Family / Backbone FoMo-Bench MultiSpectralViT (vendored local code + checkpoint loader) Adapter type on-the-fly Typical backend provider backend (gee) Primary input S2 SR 12-band (B1,B2,B3,B4,B5,B6,B7,B8,B8A,B9,B11,B12) Default resolution 10m default provider fetch (sensor.scale_m) Temporal mode range in practice (normalized via shared helper) Output modes pooled, grid Extra side inputs required modality keys (adapter provides S2 defaults, configurable via env) Training alignment (adapter path) Medium-High when S2_KEYS, normalization, and model config match checkpoint assumptions

docs.title: When To Use This Model
docs.text: FoMo is a good fit for strict multispectral S2 experiments with spectral-token modeling, for testing modality-aware token layouts beyond plain RGB ViT pipelines, and for analyses where averaging spectral tokens into one spatial grid is acceptable. The main pitfalls are changing RS_EMBED_FOMO_S2_KEYS without understanding FoMo modality indexing, treating the FoMo grid as georeferenced pixels, or modifying architecture envs while keeping an incompatible checkpoint.

docs.title: Spatial / temporal
docs.text: FoMo is provider-backed, so use backend="gee" or another provider-compatible backend. TemporalSpec is normalized through the shared helper, and TemporalSpec.range(...) is the clearest option.

docs.title: Sensor / channels
docs.text: If sensor is omitted, FoMo uses COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED with bands B1,B2,B3,B4,B5,B6,B7,B8,B8A,B9,B11,B12, scale_m=10, cloudy_pct=30, composite="median", and fill_value=0.0. If you pass input_chw, it must be CHW with C=12 in that adapter band order and raw S2 SR values in 0..10000.

docs.title: Modality keys
docs.text: The FoMo forward path requires one modality key per channel. The default S2 mapping is encoded in _DEFAULT_S2_MODALITY_KEYS, and you can override it with RS_EMBED_FOMO_S2_KEYS, which must provide exactly 12 comma-separated integers.

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline (Current rs-embed Path)
docs.text:
INPUT  provider fetch / input_chw
  -> S2 SR 12-band patch
  -> normalize with RS_EMBED_FOMO_NORM
     unit_scale: /10000
     per_tile_minmax: per-channel min-max after unit scaling
     none / raw: keep clipped raw values
  -> resize to RS_EMBED_FOMO_IMG=64
  -> load FoMo runtime + checkpoint
     vendored local runtime with local / auto-downloaded weights
  -> forward(x, spectral_keys, pool=False)
  -> token output [N,D]
  -> output projection
     pooled: mean / max over all tokens
     grid:   modality-averaged patch grid when available
     fallback: 1x1 vector grid

docs.title: Core model / preprocessing
docs.text: Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_FOMO_IMG 64 Resize target image size RS_EMBED_FOMO_PATCH 16 Patch size (used for model config + grid expectations) RS_EMBED_FOMO_NORM unit_scale unit_scale, per_tile_minmax, or none RS_EMBED_FOMO_S2_KEYS adapter S2 default mapping 12 comma-separated modality keys RS_EMBED_FOMO_FETCH_WORKERS 8 Provider prefetch workers for batch APIs

docs.title: FoMo model config (advanced; keep aligned with checkpoint)
docs.text: Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_FOMO_DIM 768 Model dim RS_EMBED_FOMO_DEPTH 12 Transformer depth RS_EMBED_FOMO_HEADS 12 Attention heads RS_EMBED_FOMO_MLP_DIM 2048 MLP dim RS_EMBED_FOMO_NUM_CLASSES 1000 Class head size (config compatibility)

docs.title: Checkpoint loading
docs.text: Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_FOMO_CKPT unset Local checkpoint path RS_EMBED_FOMO_AUTO_DOWNLOAD 1 Allow checkpoint auto-download RS_EMBED_FOMO_CACHE_DIR ~/.cache/rs_embed/fomo Checkpoint cache dir RS_EMBED_FOMO_CKPT_FILE default FoMo checkpoint filename Cached ckpt filename RS_EMBED_FOMO_CKPT_URL default Dropbox URL Checkpoint download URL RS_EMBED_FOMO_CKPT_MIN_BYTES adapter threshold Download size sanity check

docs.title: OutputSpec.pooled()
docs.text: OutputSpec.pooled() pools the FoMo token sequence across tokens. mean becomes token_mean, max becomes token_max, and metadata records token_count, token_dim, and pooling mode.

docs.title: OutputSpec.grid()
docs.text: The preferred path interprets tokens as [modalities, H, W, D], averages over modalities, and returns (D,H,W) with grid_kind="spectral_mean_patch_tokens". If token layout is incompatible with the expected modality or grid structure, the adapter falls back to a 1x1 vector grid with grid_kind="vector_as_1x1". In either case, this remains model token structure rather than georeferenced raster space.

docs.title: Minimal provider-backed example
docs.text:
from rs_embed import get_embedding, PointBuffer, TemporalSpec, OutputSpec

emb = get_embedding(
    "fomo",
    spatial=PointBuffer(lon=121.5, lat=31.2, buffer_m=2048),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2022-06-01", "2022-09-01"),
    output=OutputSpec.pooled(),
    backend="gee",
)

docs.title: Galileo (galileo)
docs.text: Multi-frame Sentinel-2 adapter that constructs Galileo encoder inputs (including months) from a temporal window and returns pooled vectors or patch-token grids.

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text: Field Value Model ID galileo Family / Backbone Galileo Encoder from vendored local runtime Adapter type on-the-fly Typical backend provider-backed; prefer backend="auto" in public API Primary input S2 10-band time series (T,C,H,W) Default resolution 10m default provider fetch (sensor.scale_m) Temporal mode range in practice (adapter normalizes via shared helper) Output modes pooled, grid Extra side inputs required months (per-frame month tokens), plus Galileo masks/tensors built by adapter Training alignment (adapter path) Medium (depends on FRAMES, IMG, PATCH, normalization)

docs.title: When To Use This Model
docs.text: Galileo is a good fit for temporal S2 sequence modeling with explicit month tokens, comparisons against other multi-frame adapters such as anysat and agrifm, and feature-grid analysis over Galileo's S2-related token groups. The main pitfalls are comparing it to single-composite models without matching temporal assumptions, changing image_size and patch_size inconsistently, or changing month handling without documenting it.

docs.title: Spatial / temporal
docs.text: The adapter accepts BBox and PointBuffer, and normalizes TemporalSpec to a range through the shared helper; TemporalSpec.range(...) is still the clearest choice for reproducibility. Galileo builds T frames by splitting the requested window into equal sub-windows and compositing one frame per bin. The months side input is derived from frame-bin midpoints unless you force a constant month with RS_EMBED_GALILEO_MONTH.

docs.title: Sensor / channels
docs.text:
If sensor is omitted, Galileo uses COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED with bands B2,B3,B4,B5,B6,B7,B8,B8A,B11,B12, scale_m=10, cloudy_pct=30, composite="median", and fill_value=0.0.

For input_chw, the adapter accepts CHW or TCHW with C=10 through the shared coercion helper. CHW repeats to T, TCHW pads or truncates to exact T, and values are clipped to the raw-SR range 0..10000.

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline (Current rs-embed Path)
docs.text:
INPUT  provider fetch / input_chw
  -> S2 10-band raw_tchw
     input_chw path: coerce to exact TCHW
  -> resolve months sequence
     frame-bin midpoints or RS_EMBED_GALILEO_MONTH override
  -> resize frames to RS_EMBED_GALILEO_IMG=64 if needed
  -> normalize series with RS_EMBED_GALILEO_NORM
     default: none
     use `official_stats` to match Galileo pretraining normalization
  -> build encoder tensors + masks
     inputs: s_t_x, sp_x, t_x, st_x
     masks:  s_t_m, sp_m, t_m, st_m
     side input: months
  -> Galileo encoder forward
     patch_size=RS_EMBED_GALILEO_PATCH=8
  -> output projection
     pooled: visible-token average
     grid:   official-style patch mean over visible tokens

Constraint:

image_size % patch_size == 0 is required.

docs.text: Env var Default Effect RS_EMBED_GALILEO_MODEL_SIZE nano Galileo model size selector (models/<size>/) RS_EMBED_GALILEO_MODEL_PATH unset Local model folder override containing config.json + encoder.pt RS_EMBED_GALILEO_HF_REPO nasaharvest/galileo Hugging Face repo used for snapshot download RS_EMBED_GALILEO_CACHE_DIR ~/.cache/rs_embed/galileo Download cache dir for model snapshots RS_EMBED_GALILEO_AUTO_DOWNLOAD 1 Auto-download model folder from Hugging Face when MODEL_PATH is unset RS_EMBED_GALILEO_IMG 64 Frame resize target RS_EMBED_GALILEO_PATCH 8 Encoder patch size RS_EMBED_GALILEO_FRAMES 8 Number of temporal frames T RS_EMBED_GALILEO_NORM none S2 normalization mode (none, unit_scale, per_tile_minmax, official_stats) RS_EMBED_GALILEO_ADD_LN 1 Add layer norm on encoder exit RS_EMBED_GALILEO_MONTH unset Force a constant month (1..12) for all frames RS_EMBED_GALILEO_FETCH_WORKERS 8 Prefetch workers for batch APIs

docs.title: OutputSpec.pooled()
docs.text: The default pooled path uses Galileo's pooled token output, recorded with token_mean semantics in metadata. If OutputSpec.pooling="max", the adapter max-pools the produced grid instead and records grid_max.

docs.title: OutputSpec.grid()
docs.text: OutputSpec.grid() returns a Galileo patch-token grid as xarray.DataArray (D,H,W). The adapter now follows Galileo's own patch-level token averaging path when available, so each spatial position is the mean of visible tokens assigned to that patch. This is model token structure rather than georeferenced raster space.
