docs.title: Compare many models in one figure
docs.text: Use the same get_embedding request for individual models, then use compare_embeddings and plot_embedding_comparison to collect a whole model selection into one figure. The figure retains every model's native grid and reports failed requests explicitly.

docs.title: A real 22-model example
docs.text:
This gallery combines 16 image encoders, three precomputed products, and three location encoders for Wuhan, China. Most panels cover [114.35, 30.48, 114.47, 30.56]; Copernicus shows its larger buffered product window. Image encoders and two products use four archived feature blocks; the three location encoders were evaluated at the same 3,072 coordinate centers for this gallery. These are genuine model outputs. No placeholder panels or generated imagery are used.

The archive is a historical qualitative diagnostic, not a new benchmark or model ranking. It intentionally shows different spatial and temporal support:

Panels Input and support Sentinel-2 reference and image encoders Historical May–October 2021 imagery; model-specific bands and native feature grids SatVision Historical MODIS proxy input, including a reflectance/LST proxy; not a strict reproduction of its original 14-band TOA input recipe Google Satellite Embedding (gse) Annual 2021 product, 1,036 × 1,336 cached samples Tessera Annual 2024 product, 863 × 1,174 cached samples Copernicus One expanded 15 km buffered query of the released 0.25° product; 3 × 2 cached samples, no requested-date semantics SatCLIP, GeoCLIP, Esri GLE Longitude/latitude only; 48 × 64 coordinate queries, with no imagery or requested date

For the image encoders, GSE, and Tessera, four neighboring blocks are arranged north to south and west to east. Each block's stored sample orientation is retained from the historical diagnostic. Where product blocks have unequal edge dimensions, missing edge cells are gray padding; feature values are never interpolated to another model's grid. Some historical encoders do not provide georeferenced token-orientation metadata, so this figure alone cannot establish pixel-level alignment.

Copernicus's historical adjacent queries returned overlapping product cells: 20 returned vectors contained only six distinct vectors. The gallery therefore shows one complete 3 × 2 query window rather than tiling repeated values into a false continuous map. Its effective query bounds are approximately [114.2236, 30.3653, 114.5364, 30.6347], larger than the other Wuhan panels.

Every panel uses its own three-component PCA projection and 2nd–98th percentile stretch. A red feature in one panel has no shared meaning with red in another. Different visual texture, feature dimensions, or apparent detail do not establish downstream accuracy. Query spacing for location encoders is sampling density, not a claim of learned physical resolution.

Download the full-resolution figure · Read the source hashes and run provenance

docs.title: Start with a small selection
docs.text:
Install the plotting extra and each selected model's runtime. Location-only examples need no imagery or Earth Engine authentication:

git clone https://github.com/GISWLH/earth-embedding.git
cd earth-embedding
pip install -e ".[plot,location]"

from earth_embedding import (
    BBox, OutputSpec, compare_embeddings, plot_embedding_comparison,
)

models = ["satclip", "geoclip", "esri_gle"]
comparison = compare_embeddings(
    models,
    spatial=BBox(114.35, 30.48, 114.47, 30.56),
    output=OutputSpec.grid(),
    grid_step_m=320,  # coordinate sampling, not image resolution
    device="cpu",
)
figure = plot_embedding_comparison(
    comparison,
    columns=3,
    save_path="location-comparison.png",
)

comparison.embeddings["esri_gle"] is the original Embedding, including its metadata. comparison.summary() reports successful shapes and errors. The default stops at an error; set on_error="record" when you want the remaining models to run and failed panels to remain visible.

docs.title: Compare the full catalog
docs.text:
models=None selects list_models(). Image encoders use a seasonal window, annual products receive a year, and location encoders ignore time. A full run requires each model's dependencies, weights, and provider access; see the model setup pages.

from earth_embedding import (
    BBox, OutputSpec, TemporalSpec,
    compare_embeddings, plot_embedding_comparison,
)

comparison = compare_embeddings(
    spatial=BBox(114.35, 30.48, 114.47, 30.56),
    temporal=TemporalSpec.range("2021-05-01", "2021-10-31"),
    output=OutputSpec.grid(),
    model_options={
        "gse": {"temporal": TemporalSpec.year(2021)},
        "tessera": {"temporal": TemporalSpec.year(2024)},
        "copernicus": {"temporal": TemporalSpec.year(2021)},
        "satclip": {"temporal": None, "grid_step_m": 320},
        "geoclip": {"temporal": None, "grid_step_m": 320},
        "esri_gle": {"temporal": None, "grid_step_m": 320},
    },
    on_error="record",
)
figure = plot_embedding_comparison(
    comparison,
    columns=5,
    save_path="all-models.png",
)
print(comparison.summary())

This is a fresh inference example; its grids and model settings need not match the archived gallery. Tessera's year is explicit because the illustrated archive uses 2024. Copernicus is a fixed released product and does not select a requested acquisition date. Model-specific options remain visible in model_options.

The comparison helper runs models sequentially and clears model runtime caches between requests by default. This limits accumulated weight memory while preserving completed embeddings. Set release_models=False when repeated calls should reuse loaded models. Large dense products can still occupy substantial memory in the returned report.

For a runnable command that saves every successful feature array, metadata, error report, and figure:

python examples/compare_models.py --models satclip geoclip esri_gle --device cpu
python examples/compare_models.py --models all --out outputs/all-models

The command exits nonzero for incomplete results unless --allow-errors is explicitly selected. Changing the model list, region, dates, or output directory does not require editing the plotting code.

docs.title: Location encoders at two scales
docs.text:
The top row evaluates 14,400 coordinate centers on a 180 × 80 longitude / latitude lattice spanning 180° W–180° E and 80° S–80° N. The bottom row evaluates the Wuhan area on a 64 × 48 lattice. All three encoders receive the same coordinates in each row. Global and local panels have independently fitted PCA colors; they are not cross-scale color matches. The smooth local fields show the models' coordinate-only behavior over a small geographic extent.

For a point list rather than an area, keep GIS longitude/latitude order:

import numpy as np
from earth_embedding import get_location_embeddings, plot_embedding_comparison

lon, lat = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(70, 140, 80), np.linspace(5, 55, 60))
points = np.column_stack([lon.ravel(), lat.ravel()])
embeddings = {
    model: get_location_embeddings(model, points, device="cpu")
    for model in ("satclip", "geoclip", "esri_gle")
}
figure = plot_embedding_comparison(
    embeddings,
    lonlat=points,
    columns=3,
    save_path="asia-location-encoders.png",
)

The (N, D) outputs preserve input order. Supplying lonlat makes the plot a spatial scatter; without coordinates it is clearly labeled as a sample strip. See SatCLIP, GeoCLIP, and Esri GLE for checkpoints, attribution, and model terms.

docs.title: Rebuild and provenance
docs.text:
From a checkout, this command rebuilds the two-scale location figure using real public checkpoints, caches the computed arrays under work/gallery-cache/, and records coordinate, feature, checkpoint, and image SHA-256 hashes:

python scripts/build_comparison_gallery.py --device cpu

The full 22-model gallery additionally needs the historical four-block feature archive, which is not bundled in this public repository:

python scripts/build_comparison_gallery.py \
  --archive /path/to/part2_model_map_figure \
  --device cpu

The archive must include blocks_2x/<model>/block_rXX_cXX.npz, corresponding JSON metadata, manifest_2x.json, and its Sentinel-2 reference PNG. The script reads those inputs without modifying them. It does not redownload image data or rerun the 19 historical image/product pipelines. Top-level Git LFS pointer files are not used as feature arrays.

The published provenance JSON records every source block and metadata hash, original model metadata, date differences, runtime versions, coordinate grids, checkpoint hashes, and the exact figure hashes. No model weights are redistributed with these illustrations.

docs.title: Real regional embeddings, maps and a CPU classifier
docs.text: The San Francisco Bay Area and surroundings span approximately 92 × 113 km (about 122.54–121.48° W, 37.30–38.32° N). The checked 2.3 MB bundle is a complete 72 × 88 grid of 6,336 real AEF 2021 cells on the official 1,280 m overview grid, with matching WorldCover 2021 reference labels and cell polygons. Every cell inside the frame is present, so maps have no clipped edges or no-data holes. This is a regional software demonstration, not a reproduction or extension of the paper's frozen 20-system global benchmark.

docs.title: Install and draw your first map
docs.text:
Python 3.12+, CPU. Install from the repository; no PyPI release is assumed.

git clone https://github.com/GISWLH/earth-embedding.git
cd earth-embedding
python -m pip install -e ".[demo,aef]"

from earth_embedding.demo import load_demo, pca_colors, plot_map
data = load_demo("aef")
colors = pca_colors(data.features)
fig = plot_map(data.samples, colors, title="San Francisco Bay Area · AEF 2021 · PCA RGB")
fig.savefig("aef-pca.png", dpi=160)

load_demo("aef") and load_demo("bayarea") load the same data without network access. Each payload is verified against SHA-256 in its bundled manifest; vectors are joined to metadata by tile_id, never an assumed file row order.

These are 1,280 m official AEF overview cells, not native 10 m point samples. Google's overviews encode normalized sums of native vectors. We decode signed int8 values using sign(x) * (x / 127.5)**2, with -128 treated as missing. RGB shows PCA components stretched at their 2nd/98th percentiles. PCA colors are not land-cover classes and cannot be compared between separately fitted maps. PCA is descriptive and is not used by the classifier. Because the sample is a complete grid (grid_row, grid_col), plot_map draws it as one seamless curvilinear mesh with exact cell geometry, cropped to the inner frame.

To reproduce official GCS reads (first call needs network access):

from earth_embedding.demo import fetch_aef_demo
fresh = fetch_aef_demo(cache_dir="cache/aef")
cached = fetch_aef_demo(cache_dir="cache/aef", offline=True)

Four bounded overview reads avoid downloading entire native COGs or a global index. The decoded array is pinned to SHA-256, then cached atomically. Raw overview payload totals 1 MiB; actual HTTP transfer includes headers and range overhead and was not metered. Network failures and corrupted caches raise clear errors without substitute data. Advanced callers can use sample_aef(points, tiles=urls, overview_level=6) directly. Omitting overview_level retains existing native 10 m behavior.

docs.title: Encode 6,336 locations with Esri GLE
docs.text:
from earth_embedding import get_location_embeddings
from earth_embedding.demo import load_demo, pca_colors, plot_map
data = load_demo("bayarea")
points = data.samples[["center_lon", "center_lat"]].to_numpy()
gle = get_location_embeddings("esri_gle", points, device="cpu", batch_size=128)
fig = plot_map(data.samples, pca_colors(gle.data), title="San Francisco Bay Area · Esri GLE · PCA RGB")
fig.savefig("esri-gle-pca.png", dpi=160)

The official lightweight Esri package (~3.7 MB) downloads once. Inference runs directly in PyTorch without ArcGIS/ArcPy. Coordinates are [longitude, latitude]. GLE has no observation year: it encodes a geographic prior. Drawing point features on this grid is a visualization choice, not matched area support. Notebook 02 verifies batch consistency and local_files_only=True. Weights are not committed and remain subject to the Esri model terms.

docs.title: Real spatial classification
docs.text:
from earth_embedding.demo import classify_demo, plot_classification
result = classify_demo()
print({k: result["metrics"][k] for k in ("oa", "macro_f1", "balanced_accuracy")})
fig = plot_classification(result)
fig.savefig("bayarea-classification.png", dpi=160)

The geographic split was fixed before scoring: two spatial folds by grid column. A model fitted only on the west half (columns 0–32) predicts the east half (columns 39–71), and a model fitted only on the east half predicts the west half. Columns 33–38 form a 7.68 km buffer that is never fitted or scored; the minimum gap between fitted and predicted footprints is 0.0737° longitude (about 6.5 km). Every scored cell therefore has an out-of-fold prediction, and the maps are complete. Two bare cells remain in the reference map but are outside the four-class task.

Fold half Built Vegetation Cropland Water Bare Total West (columns 0–32) 504 1433 51 914 2 2904 East (columns 39–71) 325 1936 512 131 0 2904 Buffer (columns 33–38) 158 299 1 70 0 528

Each fold fits StandardScaler and LogisticRegression(C=1, class_weight="balanced", tol=1e-8, max_iter=4000, random_state=42) on its own half only. Class weights compensate for the uneven cropland and water split between halves; there is no tuning or random split. Explicit float64 training and a strict convergence tolerance avoid version-dependent float32 solver paths.

Scope Scored cells OA Macro-F1 Balanced Accuracy Pooled out-of-fold 5806 93.64% 91.64% 92.63% Fit west → predict east 2904 92.46% 90.99% — Fit east → predict west 2902 94.83% 87.85% —

These are this run's measurements, saved in metrics JSON and ID-bearing predictions CSV (predicted_by names the fold model). Confusion-matrix rows are reference labels; columns are predictions, in the order built, vegetation, cropland, water. The hatched buffer is unscored. Most errors are vegetation/cropland confusions along field margins; pooled cropland recall is 470/563. Two regional folds give no uncertainty estimate or global generalization claim. WorldCover is a satellite-derived reference, not field-survey truth. Same-year products may share satellite signals, and the buffer cannot remove all spatial autocorrelation. Coarse majority classes hide within-cell mixtures.

docs.title: Sources, selection and independent rebuilding
docs.text:
The source inspection found the paper's existing global cache to be discrete samples, unsuitable for a continuous regional map. This replacement reads a bounded subset of official public products; it does not change paper data/results.

  • Google / Google DeepMind AEF GCS documentation: annual 2021, four UTM 10N COGs, official overview index 6. CC-BY-4.0.
  • ESA WorldCover data access: 2021 v200, N36W123, native 10 m labels from the official public AWS COG. CC-BY-4.0.
  • Attribution: The AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding dataset is produced by Google and Google DeepMind. © ESA WorldCover project 2021 / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021) processed by ESA WorldCover consortium.

The sample is the whole-cell rectangle x 540960–633120 m, y 4129280–4241920 m in EPSG:32610 on the official 1,280 m overview grid: 72 columns × 88 rows. It was chosen so that every cell has a complete AEF vector (open-ocean overview cells are no-data) and is checked again at build time; the earlier lon/lat-box selection clipped the rotated UTM grid into a staircase and left ocean holes. Each cell has at least 95% valid reference support. WorldCover native pixel centers inside the same AEF polygon are counted, grouped, then the most frequent group is assigned (alphabetic tie break). Codes 10/20/30/90/95/100 map to vegetation, 40 to cropland, 50 to built, 80 to water, 60 to bare and 70 to snow. Zero is nodata. Selection does not use scores. Maps use transformed polygons, including south-up source rasters; neither file order nor raster row number determines north.

The installed rs_embed/data/demos/bayarea/manifest.json records exact source URLs, pixel hashes, decoded feature hash, payload sizes, selection and license. Large source rasters are not committed. Rebuild from pinned public URLs with no private paths or index file (--repin deliberately replaces the pins):

python scripts/prepare_bayarea_demo.py
python examples/real_demos.py
python scripts/run_demo_notebooks.py
python scripts/validate_real_demos.py

Preparation reads four overviews and a bounded 12,289 × 12,728 WorldCover window (156 MB uncompressed; on-wire transfer varies). Allow a few minutes, network access and about 1 GB free memory. Source cache pixels are checked against pinned SHA-256 values. Normal examples and notebooks use only the 2.3 MB bundled subset.

Field Meaning tile_id Stable UTM center identifier, shared with NPZ feature IDs grid_row, grid_col Position in the 88 × 72 grid; row 0 is the north edge center_lon, center_lat Cell center in WGS84 degrees minlon/minlat/maxlon/maxlat Geographic envelope for split checks lon0/lat0 … lon3/lat3 Four transformed corners of the UTM cell utm_easting, utm_northing EPSG:32610 center in meters class_name, dominant_fraction Grouped majority and its fraction reference_valid_fraction Share of valid WorldCover pixels in the cell demo_split Fixed west / buffer / east fold assignment features 64-dimensional float32 official overview vectors
